original.target_description: Rosenbaum, Mama, and Algom (2017), Study 3: standing versus sitting on Stroop interference; primary original full text unavailable according to terminal acquisition record.

replication.target_description: Smith et al. (2019), Experiment 1, fourteen Washington University undergraduates, within-participant posture (sitting/standing) × congruency (neutral/congruent/incongruent) interaction on correct-trial response times in the Stroop color-word task. This matches the neutral outcome description, but the supplied p. 7 locator identifies Experiment 3 visual search rather than this Stroop test (PDF p. 3).

n.sample_role: Participants in Experiment 1 repeated-measures Stroop analysis; fourteen is printed in words and the reported F(2, 26) and t(13) are consistent with all fourteen being analyzed.
n.exclusions: No participant exclusions reported in Experiment 1; response-time analysis uses correct responses only.
n.location: p. 2321 (PDF p. 2), Experiment 1 Method—Participants; p. 2322 (PDF p. 3), Results
n.quote: Fourteen Washington University undergraduates each participated in one 30-min session for course credit.

es.location: p. 2322 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1 Results, posture × congruency interaction

p.location: p. 2322 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1 Results, posture × congruency interaction

reported_success.quote: Stroop interference was markedly reduced when participants adopted a standing posture, consistent with the Rosenbaum et al. (2017) findings.
